rules.description: Factual SCQs must be Easy and strictly within NCERT chapter limits. Understanding/Application types can refer to NCERT and PLT sources.
The solution must match the correct option. Explanations must justify the correct answer and discuss incorrect ones.
Ensure SCQ covers all textbook content. Examples may vary but must stay within chapter limits.
Image-based SCQs must be relevant, clear, and purposeful.
Use British English. Ensure technical accuracy, real-life context, and age-appropriate language to enhance critical thinking.
Assertion and Reason must be evaluated for truth and logical connection. Options must follow CBSE format (1 to 4).
Questions must map to chapters and subtopics. Minimum 4 questions per sub-topic.
RAs must be tagged to Application level (Medium/Hard). LO tagging is mandatory.
Explanations should be based on correct reasoning and clearly differentiate correct/incorrect statements.
VSAs must be based strictly on NCERT chapter content.
Allowed levels: Factual (Medium), Understanding (Easy/Medium) only. Others not permitted.
30–50 words. Can include 2 sub-parts (1 mark each).
Use NCERT-aligned vocabulary. British English only.
Do not apply LO tags. Must be tagged to chapter/sub-topic and ensure full topic coverage.
50–90 words.
Use NCERT content only. British English. External examples are allowed if conceptually valid.
3-mark questions in formats: (i) 1+1+1, (ii) 2+1, (iii) 3.
Allowed: Factual (E/M), Understanding (E/M/H), Application (M/H).
Solutions should be stepwise, clear, and numerically precise. No explanation needed. No LO tags.
Questions must require images to answer. Image relevance and clarity mandatory.
Follow formats like 2+2+1, 3+2, etc. Cognitive level based on the highest sub-question.
Strictly NCERT content. British English. Examples allowed only within conceptual scope.
Only solution is required, not explanation. No LO tags.
100–120 words across sub-questions.
Must follow NCERT formulas or image content. Visuals and numerical calculations should be conceptually aligned.
Image must match concept, add value, and be clear.
Image should deliver key information. Avoid overuse of text or hints.
Must be image-based, not text-based. Avoid distractions like filters or captions.
Include factual, understanding, and application levels. Skills like labeling and interpreting visuals.
For SA: 3 marks via 1/2/3 sub-questions. For LA: follow LA marking logic.
Can be scenario/image/data-based. Must align with NCERT content.
Avoid direct questions. Structure as 1 SA (2 marks) + 2 VSA (1 mark) or 2 SCQ (1 mark).
Must cover key concepts, multiple dimensions, and real-life relevance.
Avoid complex language. Ensure grade-appropriate tone and cognitive alignment.
SA: 50–80 words. VSA: 30–45 words.
